instruction: This design is not a rlworkbench study protocol. Implement and validate an external producer, allocate a bounded population and budget, then translate into a registered external protocol before running.
question: Do learned predictions improve the usefulness of learned options under hidden changes, beyond matched capacity, primitive experience and inference cost?

primary_outcome.normalization: none within one environment; specify weights/scales before multi-environment aggregation

required_checks: pending future targets never used early

option_contract.target: sum(D_k * reward[t+k+1], k=0..tau-1) + D_tau * continuation_value; D_k = product(gamma[t+j], j=1..k)
option_contract.boundary_rule: An option ending alone does not terminate the task. External interruption of an active option must use an algorithm-consistent continuation value.

factorial_arms.purpose: option contribution without learned GVF inputs

additional_controls: fixed or random prediction features matched in dimension and computation
fixed, random and learned option sets matched in count and duration where feasible
oracle state or model only as privileged diagnostics
fixed modules versus jointly retuned complete methods reported separately
diagnostics: option attainment, duration and behavioral redundancy
GVF x option interaction on predeclared reward scale
failure and resource growth including discarded modules

study_separation.development: independent full lifetimes for choosing learning, discovery, retirement and planning rules
study_separation.confirmation: new full lifetimes and unopened schedules after whole-procedure freeze
study_separation.prohibited: selecting questions, skills or stopping times from confirmation futures; combining the best checkpoint of every module into a fictitious system

unresolved_before_execution: specific cumulants, policies, timescales and option parameterization
all arm configs and equal-information controls
lifetime duration and complete independent seed population
interaction, computation, memory and wall-time ceilings
minimum relevant effect and statistical precision plan
failure scoring, recovery thresholds and competing-event treatment
